Today's verdict NEUTRAL-CAUTIOUS
When the signals disagree · and which one to trust
Different gauges sometimes point opposite ways. That is normal. Here is each clash in plain words, with the side to lean on for now.
⚠ These two disagree: Crash Index **1/10** — price structure reads calm vs VIX Spike Tier **2/4** at **60%** probability with skew and backwardation both active
These two can coexist: the crash index measures whether enough cross-asset signals have triggered simultaneously (none have today), while the VIX detector measures options market pricing for the next move. Skew active and backwardation active means the options market is paying for downside protection even though price hasn't broken. Trust the VIX signals as a leading indicator; the crash index tells you a disorderly move isn't happening right now, and the VIX signals tell you when right now ends.
Today's tension
Price action is quiet at Crash Index 1/10 while the options market prices a vol expansion at 60% probability.
Bull
The Crash Index sits at **1/10** and zero confluence conditions have fired. The cross-asset risk amplifiers (credit, small-caps, yen) are all quiet, which means VIX backwardation hasn't spread into a broader stress signal.
Bear
**53%** of the **43** tracked cross-asset pairs are diverging with a **19-to-4** bearish skew, and the divergence composite scores at its maximum of **100**. Internal dislocations this deep and this skewed tend to precede price dislocations, not follow them.
The tell: Watch the VIX Spike tier. If adaptive confirmation switches on and the tier moves to **3**, the gap between quiet price action and stressed options pricing closes violently.
AI read · Citrini · today's macro tape

The macro tape is calm at the surface and stressed internally. Crash Index at 1/10 and regime state STABLE at 16 say price isn't breaking. But the divergence composite is ELEVATED, 53% of the 43 tracked cross-asset pairs have broken their historical relationships, and the bearish skew runs 19-to-4. You have price holding while the internal structure deteriorates. That's compression, not stability.

Positioning should reflect that asymmetry. The contrarian score at 26 (NEUTRAL) rules out a fade setup. The macro regime is INFLATIONARY at only 45% confidence, which isn't high enough conviction to tilt hard into commodity proxies or inflation protection. You stay long the things that are leading (NDX, Korea), reduce exposure on the pairs showing the deepest correlation breaks (semis, payment processors), and watch the VIX Spike tier.

The main risk is MOVE-equity recoupling. Bond volatility and equity volatility decoupled completely: MOVE correlation with equities went from +0.71 to +0.00. If rates vol surges back into equity pricing, the Crash Index ticks up fast and the current compression unwinds. The reading that flips the stance is the VIX Spike tier moving from 2 to 3 with adaptive confirmation activating.

Cross-asset divergence radar — Cross-asset divergence watch
AI read · divergences in plain English

Divergence means assets that historically move together or apart in predictable ways have stopped doing so. When correlation drifts, the historical relationship between two instruments breaks, and those breaks tend to resolve sharply.

The composite is ELEVATED: 53% of 43 pairs are diverging with a net bearish bias of 15 (19 bearish pairs, 4 bullish), and the mother jaws score sits at its maximum of 100. The deepest breaks: MOVE (bond volatility) and equities went from +0.71 correlation to +0.00, meaning bond vol is no longer tracking equity vol at all.

USMV (the low-volatility equity ETF) flipped from -0.85 to +0.16 with SPY: defensive positioning inside equities is no longer functioning as a hedge. Energy (XLE) and gold moved from -0.44 to +0.35, two assets that normally diverge now moving together, which signals an inflation or macro overlay is taking over.

Semis (SMH) broke from SPY (+0.38 to -0.23). Visa and Mastercard, which almost always trade in lockstep, split to -0.54.

The count and depth of these breaks argue the market is actively repricing something underneath the calm price action.

Cross-Region Surveillance
Major indices from the 4 regions/asset classes. Asia trades ahead time-wise vs US — a Tokyo overnight crash often leaks into the SPX open. Crypto = 24h leading indicator of global risk appetite.
AI read · the cross-region tape

Korea leads Asia at +1.7% over five days, Australia lags at -1.6%. In Europe, the Euro Stoxx 50 gains +0.7% while the Swiss Market Index drops -1.9%.

The US sees NDX up +1.2% and the Dow down -0.7%. In crypto, ETH gains +0.5% while BTC sheds -1.8%.

The pattern across all four regions is the same: growth and technology proxies outperform while defensives and cyclicals lag. The Dow lagging NDX by 1.9 percentage points over five days is the US version of that rotation.

ETH outpacing BTC suggests crypto risk appetite is tilted toward beta, not toward a digital-gold narrative. Today's US session leader sits squarely in large-cap tech.

Crash Index — 10 lead-signal radar 1/10 · WATCH — 1-2 signals, monitoring
AI read · volatility & crash, reconciled

Crash Index at 1/10 alongside VIX Spike Tier 2/4 at 60% spike probability is a coherent state. The crash index tracks whether cross-asset risk triggers have fired simultaneously: zero of three confluence conditions are active today, so the index stays low.

The VIX Spike detector reads something different: skew is active and backwardation is active, meaning the options market is paying up for downside protection and front-month vol trades above back-month vol. Price is calm; the options market is not.

You trust the crash index for whether a disorderly move is happening right now, and you trust the VIX signals for what the market expects over the next few weeks.

Plain-English read · the Crash Index
Think of this as a smoke alarm, not a market forecast. Each of the 10 rows is a signal that led real crashes, checked over 15 years of S&P 500 history (Bonferroni-validated, so it survived a strict false-positive test). In a calm market it sits near zero by design — a low number is the alarm working, not a broken gauge. It only earns your attention when 3 or more rows light up together. Today it reads 1/10, so the tape is calm and there is no crash setup.

How to read
Each row = an independent signal Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY. The structural (DXY, SKEW, MOVE) signal a regime change over 30-90 days. The stress (HYG/IEF, VIX3M/VIX, STLFSI4) ring at 5-30 days. The triggers (SPY -2% in 5d, VIX +30% in 3d) are short-term breakouts. For a tactical decision: 3+ signals simultaneously aligned = real probability of stress, never on isolated signal (framework rule).

Heat ranking: composite of RS (relative strength vs SPY), Momentum (price action 20-60d), Breadth (% stocks above SMA), Options flow, and Attention. Use top-5 as rotation focus.
Emerging industries: high velocity = screener scores accelerating this week vs prior baseline — potential early rotation signal.
Competitor themes: token frequency × recency across top finance Substacks — useful narrative context, not a trading signal.
Best R/R: only entries with an active screener leg (PULLBACK / BOTTOM / SMART_MONEY_SURGE etc.). EV% = probabilistic edge per trade. Cross-check with weekly chart before sizing.

Reading the table — Z-Score: number of standard deviations vs rolling 100d mean. |Z| > 2 = Kerberos entry threshold, |Z| > 2.5 = extreme (best R/R on mean-reversion). %B: position within Bollinger Bands (1.0 = upper band, 0 = lower band).

Aggregate reading — the mean of Z-scores gives a global regime indicator. Positive → cross-asset overbought market (Risk-On, watch reversal). Negative → oversold (Risk-Off, possible bottoming).
How to read
Persist = number of consecutive days above |Z| > 2.0 (Kerberos threshold). Persist ≥ 3d = validated signal (the divergence has become a regime, not a spike). Persist 1-2d = to watch. Persist 0d = dead signal. Sort on this column to find established regimes worth trading.
Glossary — 18 terms to understand the dashboard
Z-Score
Number of standard deviations vs the historical mean (rolling 100 days). Z=0 = normal level · |Z|>2 = stress · |Z|>2.5 = extreme.
Bollinger Bands
Bands drawn at ±2.2σ around a 100-day moving average. When the price exits the bands = statistically extreme signal.
Backwardation
Inverted curve: immediate fear exceeds far fear (e.g. VIX > VIX3M). Short-term panic signal.
Contango
Normal situation where far fear exceeds immediate fear. Extreme contango = complacency.
Half-life
Number of days required for a gap to the mean to halve. Measures the speed of mean-reversion.
Cointegration
Two assets that move together in the long term despite short-term fluctuations. Statistical basis of pair-trading.
Mean-reversion
Strategy betting that a gap to the mean will close. Inverse of momentum (which bets on continuation).
Breadth
Width of participation in the rally. Good breadth = many stocks rising. Bad breadth = only a few mega-caps pull the index.
Hedge ratio
Quantity of asset B to short to neutralize 1 long unit of asset A. Calculated via OLS regression on historical returns.
Lead-time
Delay between a signal's appearance and the event it predicts. Structural = 30-90d · stress = 5-30d · triggers = 1-10d.
Bonferroni
Statistical correction for multiple testing. When testing 100 signals, some seem valid by chance. Bonferroni divides the significance threshold by the number of tests to eliminate these false positives.
MCPT (Monte Carlo Permutation Test)
Robustness test: data is randomly shuffled 5000-10000 times to see if the signal appears by chance. If p < 0.05, the signal is probably real.
Walk-forward
Test where the model is trained on the first years (e.g. 2010-2020) and tested on the following years (2020-2025). Avoids in-sample overfitting.
Tail-hedge
Hedge against an extreme crash (-20% or more). Bought via deeply out-of-the-money puts. SKEW measures institutional demand for this type of insurance.
Mega-caps
The 7-10 largest market caps in the SPX (AAPL, MSFT, NVDA, GOOGL, AMZN, META, TSLA). Weigh ~35% of the index.
Cap-weighted vs Equal-weighted
SPY = weighted by capitalization (mega-caps dominate). RSP = each stock weighs 0.2%. Comparing both reveals concentration.
Risk parity
Portfolio strategy that balances risk (not capital) across asset classes. Stressed when stocks/bonds correlations turn positive (inflation regime).
framework rule
Fundamental principle: a solo signal = noise, 3+ aligned signals = real edge. All panel signals are Bonferroni-validated over 15 years of SPY.
